# Golden host-to-proxy frames
#
# Produced by `just frames`. Every proxy implementation — the C receiver, the MATLAB
# reference, the Go daemon — decodes these and must agree on the values below. Three
# independent codecs is a maintenance cost worth paying only if they are pinned to a
# shared artifact, so this file is that artifact. Hex rather than binary so a change is
# reviewable in a diff.
#
# INPUT
#   dataset RID   ri.catalog.test.dataset.abc
#   channels      engine.rpm, engine.egt, engine.psi
#   session_id    0x1122334455667788
#   config_id     0x19915455f27bd0f7
#   sequence      42
#   rows          ts=1000000000  1500.0    700.0   30.0
#                 ts=1000001000  1510.5    701.5   30.1
#                 ts=1000002000  1521.25   703.0   30.2
#
# A decoder that reproduces exactly those values from the bytes below is conformant.
#
#
# config_id — get this exactly right or every frame is silently rejected
#
# FNV-1a, 64-bit, over each field length-prefixed as a 4-byte little-endian count
# followed by its bytes: first the RID, then each channel name in order.
#
#   h = 0xcbf29ce484222325                  offset basis
#   for each byte b:  h ^= b; h *= 0x100000001b3   (wrapping at 64 bits)
#
# Go has this as hash/fnv (fnv.New64a). Length-prefixing is what stops {"ab","c"} and
# {"a","bc"} colliding. Canonical check: FNV-1a/64 of the single byte 'a' is
# 0xaf63dc4c8601ec8c — verify your implementation against that before trusting it here.

config_id 19915455f27bd0f7

# Maximum channels a DATA frame can carry, derived from the 1400-byte MTU:
#   8*nch <= 1400 - 24 (header) - 12 (data fixed) - 8 (timestamp)  ->  169
# At 3 channels, 42 rows fit one datagram.
max_channels 169

# Byte order
#
# The magic is a literal byte sequence, so "NMS1" reads forwards in tcpdump. Every
# numeric field after it is LITTLE-endian, which is not the big-endian "network byte
# order" convention — that convention covers IP/TCP/UDP headers, not payloads. Both ends
# are x86-64 and the payload is mostly IEEE-754 doubles already stored little-endian, so
# big-endian would mean byte-swapping every value on the host least able to afford it.

# HELLO, 91 bytes
# 4e4d5331 magic "NMS1" | 01 version | 01 type=HELLO | 0000 reserved
# 8877665544332211 session | f7d07bf255549119 config
# 1b00 rid_len=27 | rid | 0300 channel_count=3 | (0a00 len + name) x3
hello 4e4d5331010100008877665544332211f7d07bf2555491191b0072692e636174616c6f672e746573742e646174617365742e61626303000a00656e67696e652e72706d0a00656e67696e652e6567740a00656e67696e652e707369

# DATA, 132 bytes
# header as above with type=02 | 2a00000000000000 sequence=42
# 0300 channel_count=3 | 0300 row_count=3
# then per row: 8-byte LE int64 timestamp, then channel_count 8-byte LE float64 values
data 4e4d5331010200008877665544332211f7d07bf2555491192a000000000000000300030000ca9a3b0000000000000000007097400000000000e085400000000000003e40e8cd9a3b0000000000000000009a97400000000000ec85409a99999999193e40d0d19a3b000000000000000000c597400000000000f885403333333333333e40
